summary.text: 备 is the simplified form corresponding to 備. The older graph is interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container, a scene associated with readiness; the container’s original name and any sound match remain unverified.

formation.text: 備 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 人 depicts a person, while 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container and is also assigned a sound role. The proposed carrying scene links the image with preparedness, but the pictured object’s original name and its sound match to 𤰈 are not established. The 1956 scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備.

components.text: In 備, 人 depicts the person in the proposed carrying scene associated with preparedness.

In 備, 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container, identified in texts as a quiver. It is also assigned a sound role. Zhengzhang readings for 𤰈 and 備 provide a comparison, but do not independently establish the component’s identity or role.

sound_limitation.text: The supplied Zhengzhang comparison does not independently establish 𤰈’s identity, reading, or phonetic role; the pictured object’s own original name and any match to 箙 are also unavailable.

sound.text: The reported Zhengzhang Old Chinese forms *bɯɡ for 𤰈 and *brɯɡs for 備 share an initial and similar rhyme, making a sound relationship plausible; this comparison alone does not verify the analysis.

components.text: 备 is officially adopted as the simplified form corresponding to 備. A secondary account proposes a route through variant 俻, but the official scheme does not establish that derivation.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but the supplied evidence does not date its earliest appearance. The selected descriptions are textual analyses; no glyph image was visually inspected here.

The right-hand component is printed as 𤰇 in some forms and described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. In bronze forms, its lower part is also reported to change to 用, tentatively proposed as a sound element. These accounts do not establish a complete dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 was separately recognized as a variant of 備, but the scheme does not identify it as the direct source of 备.

uncertainties.text: The proposed carrying-quiver interpretation links the graph with preparedness but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. Texts identify the pictured container as 箙, and 備 is reported as writing 箙 in a bronze inscription; neither establishes the pictured object’s original name or proves a sound match between that name and 𤰈.

備 has reported uses glossed prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver scene may help explain preparedness, but does not prove the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss 慎也 means “cautious” or “careful”; it does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” a different word. This proposed phonetic borrowing would depend on similarity between the words’ pronunciations; the evidence here does not verify that resemblance. Nor does the loan establish the pictured object’s original name or pronunciation.

overview.text: 備 is proposed to show a person carrying a quiver, a scene associated with readiness. The pictured container’s original name and any sound match are unverified. The 1956 scheme adopted 备 as the simplified form corresponding to 備; today it means “prepare” or “ready.”
